Task 5 was completed by the end of Q6 and receipt of all remaining equipment occurred in the weeks following the close of Q6. Quotes for construction and equipment purchases were updated from the initial submission to reflect the market prices at that time, which led to some increases and some decreases from the submitted budget line items. These adjustments did not affect the total project budget, and final costs were reported after invoices were processed through the vendors and the University. A balance was left for the contingency of unplanned expenses, and a plan was discussed in the quarterly meetings on August 21, 2024, and November 13, 2024, to reallocate $160,000 (10%) of the project budget from construction to equipment. This reallocation was approved, and a list of additional equipment purchases was communicated and approved in April 2025. Project Output The project received news coverage that included a feature article published through our Office of Media relations and mentions in other articles related to the Center’s research. The feature article can be found here: https://news.utdallas.edu/science-technology/wind-energy-headquarters-2024/. Lessons Learned The University supported preliminary architectural and engineering design work that took place before the project was funded. This helped to speed up and inform some of the early processes. For example, by having rough designs in place we were able to get estimates from a General Contractor that were included in the initial proposal. Once the award was granted, we were able to finalize those designs fairly quickly then get formal bids to start construction after the end of the first quarter. Additionally, having these designs made writing the Statement of Project Objectives easier with very clear scope and tasks. The changing dynamics of pricing affected purchasing equipment. Though these policy changes were not anticipated at the start of the project, their effects were felt nonetheless. In response, our team prioritized critical equipment purchases and generated purchase orders as quickly as possible while also seeking domestics sources. Vendors and suppliers were eager to meet with our team to work out solutions, however disruptions in the supply chain resulted in several delays in receiving equipment. Identifying equipment custodians, amongst faculty affiliated with the center, proved useful to procure the equipment. It is expected that these custodians will also maintain the equipment as needed.
